panels.title: Chain tip: slot number
panels.description: cardano_node_metrics_slotNum_int -- the node's current tip slot number. Climbs steadily while syncing from genesis.

panels.title: Chain tip: block number
panels.description: cardano_node_metrics_blockNum_int -- the node's current chain height.

panels.title: Block apply rate
panels.description: deriv(cardano_node_metrics_blockNum_int[2m]) -- blocks applied per second, derived from chain-height growth. dingo_ledger_block_pipeline_blocks_validated/_decoded are intentionally not used here: they stay at 0 unless the opt-in block-processing pipeline flags are set, which this stack does not enable.

panels.title: Slots behind wall clock (tip gap)
panels.description: dingo_tip_gap_slots -- slots between the current wall-clock slot and the chain tip. Trends toward 0 as sync completes and the node reaches the chain tip.

panels.title: Chainsync header cache size
panels.description: dingo_chainsync_seen_headers -- current number of slots retained in the chainsync header deduplication cache; nonzero and moving confirms active chainsync traffic.

panels.title: Block apply batch latency: p50 / p99
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.50 or 0.99, sum(rate(dingo_ledger_block_apply_batch_latency_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])) by (le)) -- wall-clock time from the start of applying one committed DB-transaction chunk of blocks to the moment its new tip is reflected in cardano_node_metrics_blockNum_int, the same gauge the 'Block apply rate' panel above derives deriv() from. This is a genuine per-batch measurement, not a per-block one: ledger/state.go commits up to 50 blocks per DB transaction and advances blockNum_int once per committed chunk, not once per block (see 'Block apply batch size' below). histogram_quantile is a bucket-boundary-bounded ESTIMATE, not an exact value; see 'Block apply batch latency: max observed' for the exact worst case. There was previously no directly-recorded latency metric consistent with the rate panel at all -- a naive 1/deriv(cardano_node_metrics_blockNum_int) derivation would derive a rate from a gauge's slope rather than record a real per-observation duration, and could not give a true percentile.

panels.title: Block apply batch latency: max observed
panels.description: dingo_ledger_block_apply_batch_max_latency_seconds -- the exact maximum wall-clock duration ever observed for dingo_ledger_block_apply_batch_latency_seconds, since process start. Monotonically non-decreasing and never resets. Unlike the p50/p99 panel above, this is not a bucket-bounded estimate: it is the precise worst-ever value, read directly from the same atomic the histogram observation updates, so it cannot drift behind the true maximum the way a separately-pushed gauge could.

panels.title: Block apply batch size
panels.description: sum(rate(dingo_ledger_block_apply_batch_size_sum[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(dingo_ledger_block_apply_batch_size_count[$__rate_interval])) -- average blocks committed per dingo_ledger_block_apply_batch_latency_seconds observation (ledger/state.go caps this at 50 blocks per DB transaction). Required context for reading the two panels above: 'batch latency / batch size' approximates the same per-block rate the 'Block apply rate' panel derives, but the latency panels themselves are per-batch, not per-block, so this shows how many blocks each observation actually covers -- a value near 1 during live tip-following, higher during bulk historical catch-up.
